main_text.head: N
main_text.p: Bado, sed: & Bajo, paenè] Pænè, nobis nigb, & well-nigb: g. in utrâq; voce superfluo, vel otiofo, & inter pronuntiandum neglecto, quin & inter scribendum perperam usurpato: à Sax. enim vocem accepimus, quibus, nih & ful-nieh scripta.
Berlando, salutare: & Berlando, liberator] Refugium, Sax.zeneh, quod ab eorum zenehian fluens, eruere, eripere, signat: hinc Dominus & Redemptor nofter, nenzeno urrep Sax. dictus.

Benwthf, Nequam: quasi dicas, nullius pretii aut ponderis] Nequitia, uti & Malitia, Sax.nyhe, & nihe: Man etiam illo sensu usurparunt: unde Nequam, Malus, eis manpulle: ; ab homini naturali nequitiâ. A nihe autem, Nequam vocárunt nihinz; Unde illud apud Mat.Parif. & alios: Rex (inquit) milites Anglos, ut ad obsidionem veniant, jubet.: nisi velint sub nomine NITHING, quod Latinè Nequam sonat, recenseri, &c. Vocabulum hoc, Nithing, thing,

page.notes: Black-letter words in the entries (headwords and Old Saxon forms) are uncertain in several places and are transcribed by best reading; the Old Saxon/Anglo-Saxon forms such as "zenehian", "nenzeno", "nyhe", "nihinz" and "ful-nieh" are doubtful. The final word "tbing," at the foot right is the continuation of the hyphenated word "Nithing" carried over from the line above; it is not a catchword. Some letters in "Nequam" and "Nithing" are rendered from a faint scan.
